I got a bit busy for reviews, but as the developer offered me a key to do so, it is only right that I do. Oh yeah - *disclaimer*.

Colony Defender is a neat little title. n short, you utilise 3 turrets, each next to a city that needs to be defended, from incoming asteroids. There's a clear 'tower defense vibe', but the random direction asteroids come towards your cities with does keep that feeling pretty limited. The level swap mixes things up a bit, with only moving spotlights giving you an idea of where the asteroids are. It can get surprisingly hectic, but it's not too hard to keep under control. For each asteroid destroyed, you net some cash, which is spent between each day on fixing up the cities or upgrading the turrets. Despite the sunshine and bunnies, it gets pretty repetitive after a while, but will, actually, forever sit on my desktop for when I have 5 minutes to kill.

**3/10: The novelty wears off fairly quickly, but for a cheap indie title, it's mildly entertaining for what it's worth, and a pretty decent accomplishment for a first time developer.**

Colony Defender is available [here](http://www.mfafbgames.com/colonydefender.html).
